metadata.dcterms:title: Sum rule for the Compton amplitude and implications for the proton–neutron mass difference
metadata.dcterms:creator: Gasser1, J.
Leutwyler1, H.
Rusetsky2, A.
a
metadata.dcterms:abstract: The Cottingham formula expresses the leading contribution of the electromagnetic interaction to the proton- neutron mass difference as an integral over the forward Compton amplitude. Since quarks and gluons reggeize, the dispersive representation of this amplitude requires a sub- traction. We assume that the asymptotic behaviour is dom- inated by Reggeon exchange. This leads to a sum rule that expresses the subtraction function in terms of measurable quantities. The evaluation of this sum rule leads to m p−n QED = 0.58 ± 0.16 MeV.
